name: REGEXMATCH
description: REGEXMATCH checks whether a text string matches a regular expression pattern and returns TRUE or FALSE.
tldr: REGEXMATCH returns TRUE if the text matches a regular expression pattern, otherwise FALSE.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text to test against the regular expression.

parameters.name: regular_expression
parameters.description: The RE2 regular expression pattern to match. Some metacharacters need escaping.

basicExample.description: Check if an email address looks valid
basicExample.explanation: The pattern checks for a typical email format. It returns TRUE if A2 matches.

advancedExamples.title: Check for a phone number pattern
advancedExamples.description: Detect if a cell contains a 10-digit US phone number
advancedExamples.result: TRUE if a phone number is found
advancedExamples.explanation: The pattern looks for three digits, a hyphen, three digits, a hyphen, and four digits.

advancedExamples.title: Match whole column with ARRAYFORMULA
advancedExamples.description: Check every cell in a column for a valid code format
advancedExamples.explanation: ARRAYFORMULA applies REGEXMATCH to each row.

howItWorks: REGEXMATCH evaluates the text against a regular expression using the RE2 syntax. It returns TRUE if the text contains a match anywhere (unless anchored), and FALSE otherwise. The pattern is case-sensitive by default.

howToSteps.name: Write the text or reference
howToSteps.text: Select the cell containing the text to test.

howToSteps.name: Build the regex pattern
howToSteps.text: Create a regular expression that describes the pattern you want to match.

howToSteps.name: Use with IF or FILTER
howToSteps.text: Wrap with IF to return custom messages, or use FILTER to extract matching rows.

limitations: REGEXMATCH is Google Sheets only. Excel uses ISNUMBER(SEARCH(...)) or VBA/User-Defined Functions for regex.
It uses RE2 syntax, which does not support all features of PCRE or .NET regex.
Lookahead and lookbehind assertions are not supported in RE2.
The pattern is case-sensitive; use character classes like [A-Za-z] for case-insensitive matching.

commonErrors.cause: The regular expression is invalid or uses unsupported syntax.
commonErrors.fix: Test the pattern in a regex tester and ensure it uses RE2-compatible syntax.

commonErrors.cause: The pattern matches part of the text because it is not anchored.
commonErrors.fix: Add ^ at the start and $ at the end to match the entire string.
Use character classes like [A-Za-z] or convert the text with LOWER/UPPER first.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: REGEXMATCH is exclusive to Google Sheets. Excel does not have a built-in regex function.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: In Excel, use SEARCH with wildcards or Power Query for pattern matching.

faq.question: Can REGEXMATCH return the matched text?
faq.answer: No, it returns only TRUE or FALSE. Use REGEXEXTRACT to capture matched text.

faq.question: Is REGEXMATCH case-sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. Use [A-Za-z] or LOWER/UPPER to handle case.

faq.question: Can I use REGEXMATCH in Excel?
faq.answer: Excel does not have a built-in REGEXMATCH function. You can use VBA or Office Scripts.

faq.question: Does it support capture groups?
faq.answer: No, REGEXMATCH only checks for a match. Use REGEXEXTRACT for capture groups.
